newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia ex-communist wins parliament seat.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia ex-communist wins parliament seat.

text.p: The leader of Mongolia's ex-communist opposition party won a crucial by-election on Monday, leaving the ruling democrats one seat short of the two-thirds majority needed to override a presidential veto.

Preliminary results for Sunday's election in western Zavkhan province showed the Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party (MPRP) leader N. Enkhbayar won 71.1 percent of the vote in the traditional ex-communist stronghold, local election committee officials said.
The candidate of the ruling Democratic Union Coalition, B. Tsenddoo, recorded 19.8 percent of the vote, officials said. Two candidates from smaller parties took the rest of the vote.
The seat fell vacant last June when incumbent opposition leader Natsagiin Bagabandi won election as state president.

The opposition win did not change the balance of power in the 76-seat Great Hural, or parliament, where the ruling coalition holds 50 seats to 25 for the opposition MPRP. One seat is held by the small Traditional United Party.
"We participated in the election with success," a MPRP spokesman told a news conference. "The opposition will remain strong."
Enkhbayar, 39, was minister of culture until the former communists were ousted in general elections last year.

The ruling coalition had been hoping to win the seat to give it the two-thirds majority it needs to override a presidential veto. Mongolia's president is largely a figurehead, but can block legislation for a period.
